candidates.title: Tech stocks slide as AI slowdown debate reaches markets
candidates.whyItMayWork: Connects a highly current AI-safety debate directly to chip and tech valuations; strong finance-community explainer angle.
candidates.whyItMayBeWeak: Market moves are fast-changing and causal attribution is contested; every price/index claim needs a timestamp and careful wording.
candidates.followUpOrComments: Follow-up through current market data and primary executive statements; no canonical social engagement observed.
candidates.images: No article or market-chart media copied; reuse rights unresolved.

candidates.title: Former DeepMind researcher raises severe AI-risk warning after leaving
candidates.whyItMayWork: Personal career decision plus a major AI-safety argument gives a clear people-first story rather than another abstract model announcement.
candidates.whyItMayBeWeak: The headline language is extreme; production must attribute the claim to the researcher and avoid presenting it as established fact.
candidates.followUpOrComments: Article references public X and LinkedIn statements; direct engagement counts were not observed in this run.

candidates.title: Gates Foundation pairs AI inequality warning with $1B access pledge

candidates.whyItMayBeWeak: Needs primary foundation material before converting the pledge details into production claims; avoid promotional framing.
candidates.followUpOrComments: Primary foundation announcement should be checked before production; no canonical social engagement observed.

candidates.title: NYC council members propose restricting YouTube in schools

candidates.followUpOrComments: Follow-up should use council/education-department primary material; no canonical social engagement observed.
